The Solar Topps Difference
Locally Owned | Fast Installs | No Subcontractors | 25 Year Warranties | 5-Star Support | A+ BBB Rated
Based in Phoenix since 2009, our lowest-priced, premium solar energy solutions provide the best value in Solar, Battery Backup and EV Charging options. We’ve helped thousands of Arizonans happily make the switch to solar and we want to do the same for you!
We aren’t just roofers, electricians, or salespeople who decided to get into the solar industry. We are a highly accredited construction engineering firm that specializes in designing, installing, and servicing rooftop, ground mount, and shade structure solar systems for homes and businesses.
Our reputation as Arizona’s Most Trusted Solar Company is because of our recognition within the industry as a true leader, our award-winning project management operation, our consistently over-performing systems, and prompt, exceptional customer service when you need it. As a proud, locally owned, all-in-one solar company, we provide premium products that are precisely engineered and installed to deliver premium results.
Better Products. Better Service. Always For a Lower Price.
Who We AreWe Are Arizona’s Trusted Leader in Solar + Battery Solutions
Trusted for our proven results, we’re continuously ranked among Arizona’s most reputable solar and battery installers. We provide industry-leading products, installations and service to help maximize savings.
Solutions Engineered Around Your Needs
At Solar Topps, we deliver fully customized energy solutions designed to maximize savings and improve energy independence for homeowners and businesses. Whether you’re considering a new solar installation, expanding your existing solar system, or adding a battery-only backup for uninterrupted power, our team builds the perfect system tailored to your needs. Because all of our design, engineering, installation, and support services are completed in-house, you receive better efficiency, faster turnaround, and superior quality control. This in-house versatility allows us to create solar and battery systems that are optimized for performance, long-term reliability, and return on investment—not one-size-fits-all packages.
With Solar Topps, your future-ready energy solution is backed by experienced professionals who take full ownership—from design and installation to long-term support.

Get Whole-Home Backup at the Lowest Cost Ever - No Solar Needed!
Charge your battery from the grid when energy is cheapest and protect your home from rate hikes, peak pricing, demand fees and unpredictable power outages. Lower your utility bill and offset rising electricity costs with a battery-only energy system from Solar Topps. Whether a new installation or an addition to an existing system, we’ve got you covered.
Contact for a Free Site EvaluationExciting Company Updates
Now Offering Battery Only Installs!
Protect your home from unexpected power outages with a battery backup system—no solar panels required! You can store power from the grid when energ is cheapest and then use it to stay powered during blackouts, storms, or grid failures, keeping your lights, appliances, and essential devices running seamlessly. Unlike traditional generators, battery backups are quiet, maintenance-free, and provide instant power without the need for fuel. Plus, they help you save money by storing energy when rates are low and using it during peak hours. Don’t wait for the next outage—invest in reliable backup power today and enjoy peace of mind knowing your home is always protected.

Jason
1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from...
1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.
Thanks, Niel, Sean, Robby, Summy, Mike, Gaurav
I have turned into a total solar geek. Thanks Solar Topps!!!!

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

Solar Topps gave us a price equal to the lowest national quote and the hardware was better (Panasonic panels versus something else) and good Enphase electronics. They were also a couple thousand dollars less than another local company we had install our solar hot water heater system.
We had a signed contract with Solar Topps dated March 9 and our system was turned on and working April 12.
That, to us, is an incredibly fast turnaround for a good sized solar panel system. We had been prepared by other companies for a 90 day period of time start to finish, so to have it done in a few days more than A MONTH was a very pleasant surprise.
We didn't have to do ANY of the paperwork with Maricopa County or APS, Solar Topps took care of all of it in a painless fashion.
Solar Topps was a pleasure to work with every step of the way. Any questions were answered via phone or email VERY promptly and correctly.
An example:
Our system has panels oriented south and west. Solar Topps was the only company to come up with this option to maximize the efficiency of our system to take advantage of the peak power rates of APS by having some panels installed to maximize the efficiency of the total system in the afternoon when the sun is lower in the west. See the attached real-time report from our panels and an early billing report from APS where our first few days with the system running has APS paying US instead of vice-versa. (to be fair, the weather has been easy and the A/C hasn't been running, but... still that's pretty cool)
If you are thinking of solar and you're in the Phoenix metro area (or elsewhere, even), you should definitely give SERIOUS consideration to using local company around for a long time Solar Topps.
Seriously, DO IT!

Solar Topps is Arizona’s Solar and Battery Backup Company. As a proudly local, fully integrated solar provider, we don’t just install systems—we build lasting partnerships rooted in trust, expertise, and accountability. Every part of our operation is handled in-house, allowing us to maintain complete control over quality, timelines, and outcomes. Our team is thoroughly trained across every function, ensuring each solar system is designed, installed, and supported with unmatched precision and industry-exceeding standards.
What truly sets Solar Topps apart is our proactive approach. We’ve spent years cultivating strong working relationships with utilities, city permitting offices, and HOAs across Arizona, which allows us to anticipate challenges, eliminate unnecessary delays, and keep projects moving forward smoothly. This behind-the-scenes expertise translates into a more efficient experience for our customers—and fewer surprises along the way.
Equally important is our commitment to the people we serve. From the first conversation to long after your system is energized, our focus is on your experience. We take the time to educate, communicate clearly, and address concerns before they become problems. Our goal is to minimize downtime, maximize performance, and ensure you feel confident and supported at every stage of the solar journey.
At the core of Solar Topps is a relentless customer-first mindset. Whether you’re just beginning to explore solar, navigating an upgrade or expansion, or curious about the latest advancements in solar and battery technology, our team is always accessible and ready to help. With more than a decade of experience serving Arizona homeowners and businesses, we understand the unique demands of our state—and we take pride in delivering solutions built to last.
As your local solar and battery backup partner, we are deeply invested in our community and in every system we install. When you choose Solar Topps, you’re choosing proven expertise, transparent communication, and a company that stands behind its work—before, during, and long after installation. Because to us, you’re not just a customer—you’re our neighbor, and your trust means everything.
Trusted for our proven results, we’re continuously ranked among Arizona’s most reputable solar and battery installers. We provide industry-leading products, installations and service to help maximize savings.
Being family-owned means we answer to our customers—not investors or corporate shareholders. Our decades-long presence in Arizona reflects proven reliability, consistent quality, and true accountability. Unlike national installers that often outsource work or exit markets, Solar Topps is local and established, reducing risk and ensuring long-term support. When you choose us, you gain a trusted solar and battery partner committed to standing behind your system for its entire lifespan.
Being engineering-focused means your system is designed for performance, reliability, and long-term value—not shortcuts. Our in-house engineers carefully evaluate your home, energy usage, and future needs to deliver optimized solar and battery solutions. Unlike many national installers that rely on standardized templates and outsourced design, Solar Topps takes a performance-driven approach to ensure your system produces more, lasts longer, and performs exactly as promised.
Our systems are installed exclusively by highly trained, in-house professionals—never subcontractors. This ensures consistent quality, accountability, and craftsmanship on every project. Unlike national installers that often rely on third-party crews with varying standards, Solar Topps maintains full control over training, safety, and execution, delivering a smoother installation experience and a system you can trust from day one.
We stock our materials locally and maintain in-house service teams so we can respond fast—often dispatching technicians to your home within hours, not days or weeks. This allows us to quickly resolve issues, minimize downtime, and keep your system performing at its best. Unlike national installers that rely on remote scheduling, third-party warehouses, and long service queues, Solar Topps is built for speed, responsiveness, and real-time support when it matters most.

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from...
1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.
Thanks, Niel, Sean, Robby, Summy, Mike, Gaurav
I have turned into a total solar geek. Thanks Solar Topps!!!!

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

With industry-leading performance and real-time tracking technology, solar puts you in full control of how, when, and where your energy is used. Monitor your production and consumption from your phone, optimize usage during peak hours, and make smarter decisions that directly lower your monthly costs. Instead of relying on a utility company to manage your power, you gain visibility and control over your home’s energy ecosystem—helping you waste less, save more, and maximize the value of every kilowatt your system produces.
Extreme weather events, grid failures, and rolling blackouts are becoming more common—but your home doesn’t have to be vulnerable. With solar (and optional battery backup), your family can keep essential systems running even when the grid goes down: Lights stay on; Refrigeration stays cold; Wi-Fi stays connected. That peace of mind is priceless—especially when your neighbors are left in the dark. Solar gives you confidence that your home is prepared, resilient, and protected no matter what’s happening outside.
Why keep renting power from the utility company at ever-increasing rates? Solar allows you to produce the same energy they provide—but at a fraction of the cost. Homeowners can reduce their electric bills by up to 80% or more, while locking in predictable energy costs for decades. Instead of being exposed to inflation, fuel price spikes, and rate hikes, your monthly energy expense becomes stable and controllable.
Solar doesn’t just save money—it adds value. In most cases, homes with solar sell faster and attract more buyers, as energy-efficient, lower-cost homes are increasingly in demand. Buyers recognize the long-term savings and sustainability benefits, making solar a powerful differentiator in today’s real estate market. Whether you plan to stay for years or sell down the road, solar helps position your home as a modern, forward-thinking investment.

We provide industry-leading coverage so that your home and system

At Solar Topps, we specialize in residential energy energy solutions that help homeowners lower electricity bills, increase energy independence, and protect their homes from rising utility rates and power outages. Whether you’re ready for a new home solar installation, expanding an existing residential solar system, or adding a solar battery backup for uninterrupted power, we design the ideal solution for your home’s specific needs.
Unlike many solar companies that outsource key steps, Solar Topps handles all design, engineering, installation, and support in-house. This means you get faster project completion, higher-quality workmanship, and a system that’s built to perform efficiently in Arizona’s demanding climate. Our end-to-end in-house approach allows us to create high-performance solar and battery systems that deliver long-term reliability, maximum savings, and a stronger return on investment. No generic, one-size-fits-all packages—only custom solar solutions built for your home.
If you’re searching for a trusted residential solar company in Arizona, Solar Topps delivers future-ready home energy systems backed by experts who support you at every step.
Our proven track record of superior engineering, high-quality installations and
excellent customer service has earned us the highest certifications in the industry.
Since 2009, Arizona homeowners have trusted Solar Topps as a leader in residential solar installations. From day one, we have maintained our North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners (NABCEP) certification—setting the standard for ethical design, engineering, and installation. What truly sets us apart is our commitment to honesty: if solar isn’t the right solution for your home, usage, or budget, we’ll tell you. We believe long-term trust matters more than a quick sale. That integrity is why we’re recognized as a Salt River Project (SRP) Preferred Solar Installer and an Arizona Public Service (APS) Qualified Technology Installer.
That same trust extends to the industry’s most respected manufacturers. Solar Topps is a Tesla Powerwall Certified Installer, Enphase Gold Installer, REC Certified Solar Professional Installer, and **Panasonic Elite Installer—credentials reserved for companies that consistently deliver exceptional quality and customer satisfaction. With a fully stocked local warehouse, we’re able to install faster, respond quicker, and support our customers without delays.
Most importantly, every Solar Topps system is designed, installed, and serviced by our own in-house team—never subcontractors. This gives us complete control over workmanship, cleanliness, and system performance, allowing us to confidently stand behind our work with 25-year Total System Protection warranties. From your first consultation through decades of ownership, Solar Topps delivers peace of mind, accountability, and solar + battery installs done the right way.
We Promise to Always Do Right By You

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from...
1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.
Thanks, Niel, Sean, Robby, Summy, Mike, Gaurav
I have turned into a total solar geek. Thanks Solar Topps!!!!

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

We nearly signed a contract with a national company and hesitated once we found out they didn't have a local subcontractor to actually install the system and would, instead, have a company travel from Tucson to Cave Creek.
We contacted a few local companies and also used Energy Sage online to get some quotes. Two responses from Energy Sage included Solar Topps and we're glad they did.
Solar Topps gave us a price equal to the lowest national quote and the hardware was better (Panasonic panels versus something else) and good Enphase electronics. They were also a couple thousand dollars less than another local company we had install our solar hot water heater system.
We had a signed contract with Solar Topps dated March 9 and our system was turned on and working April 12.
That, to us, is an incredibly fast turnaround for a good sized solar panel system. We had been prepared by other companies for a 90 day period of time start to finish, so to have it done in a few days more than A MONTH was a very pleasant surprise.
We didn't have to do ANY of the paperwork with Maricopa County or APS, Solar Topps took care of all of it in a painless fashion.
Solar Topps was a pleasure to work with every step of the way. Any questions were answered via phone or email VERY promptly and correctly.
An example:
Our system has panels oriented south and west. Solar Topps was the only company to come up with this option to maximize the efficiency of our system to take advantage of the peak power rates of APS by having some panels installed to maximize the efficiency of the total system in the afternoon when the sun is lower in the west. See the attached real-time report from our panels and an early billing report from APS where our first few days with the system running has APS paying US instead of vice-versa. (to be fair, the weather has been easy and the A/C hasn't been running, but... still that's pretty cool)
If you are thinking of solar and you're in the Phoenix metro area (or elsewhere, even), you should definitely give SERIOUS consideration to using local company around for a long time Solar Topps.
Seriously, DO IT!

Return on Investment
Your rooftop is one of the most underutilized assets on your property. Commercial rooftop solar transforms offices, warehouses, and manufacturing facilities into on-site power plants—reducing operating expenses while increasing long-term asset value. By generating clean energy directly where it’s consumed, businesses can significantly offset utility costs, stabilize energy expenses, and protect against unpredictable rate increases. With minimal disruption to daily operations and scalable system designs, rooftop solar is one of the fastest ways to improve cash flow and sustainability metrics at the same time.
Solar carports and shade structures allow your parking areas to do double duty—producing energy while providing valuable shade and weather protection for employees and customers. These systems improve comfort, reduce heat exposure, and elevate the visual appeal of your property, all while contributing to meaningful energy savings. For customer-facing businesses, solar carports also signal environmental leadership and innovation—enhancing brand perception without sacrificing function.
The top level of your parking garage is prime real estate—yet it often goes unused. Solar canopies turn that space into a high-performing energy asset while improving vehicle protection and user comfort. By integrating solar into parking structures, owners can create a new revenue stream, offset facility energy costs, and extend the life of parked vehicles by reducing heat exposure. It’s a strategic upgrade that increases both functional and financial performance of your existing infrastructure.
Energy storage allows businesses to capture excess solar production and deploy it when it matters most—during peak demand hours, utility rate spikes, or grid disruptions. By pairing solar with battery storage, companies can reduce demand charges, improve energy reliability, and maintain operations during outages. Storage also provides flexibility, enabling you to optimize energy usage day or night while strengthening resilience across your facilities.

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from...
1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.
Thanks, Niel, Sean, Robby, Summy, Mike, Gaurav
I have turned into a total solar geek. Thanks Solar Topps!!!!

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

Our system has panels oriented south and west. Protect yourself from increasing electricity costs! A battery can charge during cheaper (off-peak) periods and discharge when electricity is most expensive. This means you can continue to save money without compromising comfort.
Grid outages are becoming more frequent due to aging infrastructure. A standalone battery can provide seamless backup power for critical appliances like refrigerators, medical devices, lights, or the internet.
No solar? No problem. Our standalone battery systems connect directly to the grid, offering flexibility and reliability that fits your unique needs. You can now stay powered and connected—no generator, no noise, no fumes.
Charge your battery from the grid when energy is cheapest and protect your home from rate hikes, peak pricing, demand fees and unpredictable power outages. Lower your utility bill and offset rising electricity costs with a battery-only energy system from Solar Topps. Whether a new installation or an addition to an existing system, we’ve got you covered.

A battery backup system stores energy from the grid with your solar panels. During a power outage or instances of high energy demand, the system switches to the stored energy. Modern battery backup solutions are equipped with intelligent monitoring and management features. These systems are scalable and can be customized to meet the specific energy needs of both Arizona residential and commercial setups.
The lifespan of solar batteries depends on several factors, including the battery type, usage patterns, and maintenance practices. Generally, most high-quality solar batteries last between 5 to 15 years. Lithium-ion batteries, which are widely used in modern energy storage systems, tend to have a longer lifespan and higher efficiency compared to traditional lead-acid batteries.
Proper charging and discharging cycles, along with protecting the battery from extreme temperatures, can significantly enhance its durability. Regular maintenance and monitoring are also essential to ensure optimal performance and prolong the battery’s operational life. When selecting a solar battery, it is crucial to consider the warranty and life expectancy provided by the manufacturer, as these can serve as indicators of the battery’s quality and reliability.
Backup duration depends on your energy consumption and the specific battery model. Typically, batteries can power essential appliances for several hours to a full day. However, it is important to note that as the battery gets older, its capacity and backup duration may decrease. Regular maintenance and monitoring of your battery system can help you anticipate any potential issues and ensure that it continues to function effectively during an outage.
To make sure your battery backup system functions during an outage, regular maintenance is key. This includes checking the charge level of your batteries periodically and replacing them as needed. It’s also important to keep the batteries clean and free from debris or corrosion.
Furthermore, it’s crucial to have a qualified professional like Solar Topps inspect and service your battery backup system every year.

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

Look at your household’s current electricity needs — including everyday usage and new demands like electric vehicle (EV) charging. If your energy use is rising (or you expect it will), adding panels can help you keep pace without relying more on the grid.
Compare how much power your current system produces to how much you use. If there’s a gap — especially during peak hours — extra panels can help you cover the difference and avoid costly utility power.
Adding panels to an existing system is typically far more cost-effective than installing a brand-new setup. Plus state incentives and utility rebates can significantly reduce your out-of-pocket expense.
Every year, utilities raise their rates. Expanding your solar system now locks in more of your own power production and protects you from future price hikes — while potentially increasing your home’s value.
As energy needs grow and utility rates continue to rise across Arizona, many homeowners are expanding their solar systems to keep up. Whether you’re charging an EV, adding new air conditioners, working from home, or simply using more electricity, your original system may no longer meet your household’s demand.

Adding more solar panels to your system can lead to significant long-term savings. By generating more electricity on-site, you can significantly lower your reliance on the utility grid, reducing energy bills. Increased production may also qualify you for net metering, allowing excess energy to earn credits on future bills. Expanding your system can boost energy resilience, especially with battery storage, providing reliable backup during outages or peak demand while offering both financial and practical benefits.
Absolutely! Arizona’s climate, characterized by abundant sunshine, makes it an ideal location to maximize the benefits of solar energy system expansion. By adding more solar panels, residents can further capitalize on this renewable resource, achieving greater energy independence and contributing to a more sustainable future.
With the state’s various incentives, such as tax credits and rebate programs, the cost of increasing solar capacity is offset, ensuring a quicker return on investment. For homeowners and businesses alike in Arizona, the long-term savings and environmental advantages make solar panel expansion a strategic and impactful decision.
Adding more solar panels can greatly help with charging an Electric Vehicle (EV) in Arizona. Increasing your solar system’s capacity generates more renewable energy during the day, reducing your reliance on grid electricity and lowering costs and your carbon footprint.
With enough solar capacity and a home battery, you can store excess energy for nighttime EV charging, maximizing efficiency and sustainability. Proper planning is essential to ensure your solar setup meets household and EV charging needs.
Adding solar panels to your property can have varying impacts on property taxes depending on local laws and regulations. Arizona offers tax incentives or exemptions for installing solar energy systems. These exemptions often mean that while solar panels may increase the value of your home, this added value is not subject to higher property taxes.
It’s important to research and understand your local tax policies in your Arizona City or consult with a tax professional to determine how solar panel installation might affect your property taxes. Taking advantage of these incentives can make transitioning to renewable energy more affordable and financially beneficial.
Regular cleaning of solar panels is essential to maintain their efficiency and maximize energy output. The frequency of cleaning largely depends on the location and environmental conditions. For instance, solar panels installed in areas with minimal rainfall or high levels of dust, pollen, or bird droppings may require cleaning every few months.
We recommend visually inspecting panels periodically and cleaning them whenever significant dirt or debris is observed. Proper cleaning techniques, such as using non-abrasive materials and distilled water, can prevent damage and ensure optimal performance.
Solar Topps offers comprehensive maintenance services designed to keep your solar panels operating at peak efficiency. Our team of experienced professionals ensures that your panels are thoroughly inspected and cleaned using safe, effective methods to help troubleshoot your solar energy system. By leveraging our expertise, we help identify potential issues early and implement solutions that extend the lifespan of your solar system.

Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

When your panels produce more energy than your home needs, a battery allows you to store it instead of sending it back to the grid for minimal credit. This means more of the power you generate stays in your home and works directly for you. By using stored solar energy during high-demand times, you get a higher return on every kilowatt your system produces. Adding a battery ensures you get the most from your existing solar investment.
A battery lets you store the excess solar energy your system already produces and use it during expensive peak-rate hours. This helps you avoid costly demand charges and reduces your reliance on unpredictable utility prices. With more control over when and how your energy is used, your monthly bills become more stable and predictable. Over time, this strategic energy use can significantly increase your savings.
A battery keeps your home powered during outages, so you’re never left in the dark when the grid fails. It automatically kicks in the moment power is lost, keeping essential appliances and devices running. This added reliability gives you confidence during storms, equipment failures, or unexpected grid issues. With a battery, your home stays safe, comfortable, and connected no matter what’s happening outside.
Charge your battery from the grid when energy is cheapest and protect your home from rate hikes, peak pricing, demand fees and unpredictable power outages. Lower your utility bill and offset rising electricity costs with a battery-only energy system from Solar Topps. Whether a new installation or an addition to an existing system, we’ve got you covered.

A battery backup system works by storing electricity from the grid or renewable energy sources, like solar panels, for later use. During a power outage or instances of high energy demand, the system automatically switches to the stored energy, ensuring continuous power supply to critical appliances or systems. Modern battery backup solutions are equipped with intelligent monitoring and management features, allowing you to optimize energy usage, reduce utility costs, and maintain power during emergencies. These systems are scalable and can be customized to meet the specific energy needs of both residential and commercial setups.
The cost of adding a battery to an existing solar energy system can vary based on several factors, including battery type, storage capacity, installation requirements, and your location. Here’s a detailed breakdown of what generally what you can generally expect, but since we customize each job, it’s important to get an accurate quote:
Installing solar batteries, like the Tesla Powerwall 3, can start from around $10,000. About 10% of this cost goes towards installation and permitting requirements. Financial incentives, such as the U.S. Federal Tax Credit, can reduce upfront expenses by 30%. Solar batteries offer long-term savings by lowering electricity bills, especially in areas with high energy rates, making them a smart move toward energy independence.
Adding a battery to an existing solar energy system can play a critical role in mitigating the impact of energy blackouts. When paired with a solar panel system, these batteries store excess energy produced during the day, during peak hours. Using lower-cost, stored energy rather than expensive, utility energy is peak-shaving.
Battery technology can transition to backup power during an outage, making it a reliable solution for regions prone to frequent blackouts. By integrating batteries into an existing solar energy system, Arizona homeowners and businesses reduce their reliance on APS and SRP.
Batteries for solar energy systems come in three main types: lithium-ion, lead-acid, and flow batteries.
Lithium-Ion: Efficient, long-lasting, and ideal for daily use, though more expensive upfront.
Lead-Acid: Affordable, used off-grid, but with a shorter lifespan and lower energy density.
Flow Batteries: Scalable and durable, suited for large-scale storage, not for residential use.
Choosing the right battery depends on your energy needs, balancing cost, efficiency, and longevity.

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from...
1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.
Thanks, Niel, Sean, Robby, Summy, Mike, Gaurav
I have turned into a total solar geek. Thanks Solar Topps!!!!

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

We had a signed contract with Solar Topps dated March 9 and our system was turned on and working April 12.

An example:
Our system has panels oriented south and west. Solar Topps was the only company to come up with this option to maximize the efficiency of our system to take advantage of the peak power rates of APS by having some panels installed to maximize the efficiency of the total system in the afternoon when the sun is lower in the west. Over time, solar panels naturally degrade and may produce less electricity. If you notice a significant drop in system output that can’t be explained by shading or inverter issues, it may be time to evaluate a solar panel replacement or system upgrade.
Severe weather events—such as hailstorms, high winds, lightning strikes, or debris impact—can crack panels or damage internal components. Even minor damage can reduce efficiency or create safety concerns, making replacement the best long-term solution.
Solar technology has advanced rapidly in recent years. Older panels may lack today’s higher efficiency ratings, improved durability, sleeker designs, and better performance in low-light conditions. Replacing aging panels can significantly increase energy production without expanding roof space.
Even well-maintained panels eventually reach the end of their productive lifespan. If your system is approaching or beyond its warranty period, solar panel replacement can help restore reliability and maximize your return on investment.
When it comes to solar panel replacement, homeowners trust Solar Topps because we remove uncertainty from the process. Unlike many installers who face long equipment delays, we maintain strong stock availability of top-tier solar panels and components—allowing us to replace damaged or aging panels quickly without putting your system offline for weeks or months.
Our team is known for exceptional service, fast response times, and clear communication, so you’re never left wondering what’s happening with your system. From the initial assessment to final inspection, everything is handled in-house by experienced professionals, ensuring quality control, faster timelines, and a smoother overall experience. When your solar production matters, Solar Topps delivers reliable solutions—promptly, professionally, and without compromise.
Our proven track record of superior engineering, high-quality installations and
excellent customer service has earned us the highest certifications in the industry.
Replacing Solar Panels comes with significant benefits that enhance both energy efficiency and satisfaction. These include:
Improved Energy Output: New technology delivers enhanced performance, higher-wattage panels, and improved energy conversion rates.
Lower Energy Bills: A more efficient system means you’ll rely less on energy from the grid, cutting electricity costs further.
Modern Features: Enjoy benefits like smartphone-connected monitoring and advanced durability features that handle extreme weather conditions.
Higher Property Value: Upgrading your solar system makes your home more attractive to eco-conscious buyers and boosts marketability.
The timeframe for replacing solar panels depends on several factors, such as the size of the system. The complexity of the installation and the availability of replacement panels are also important. On average, the process can take anywhere from one to three days. We remove the Existing Solar Panels, inspecting the mounting structure and electrical connections. We install the new panels shortly after.
Solar panels are designed to be highly durable and typically have a lifespan of 25 to 30 years. But their efficiency may decline over time due to exposure to weather conditions, wear and tear, or advancements in solar technology. We watch the performance of your solar energy system to identify any drops in efficiency.
Factors such as physical damage, inverter malfunctions, or significant reductions in energy output may show the need for a replacement. Regular maintenance and professional inspections can help extend the lifespan of your solar panels and ensure consistent performance.
A solar inverter can malfunction due to various reasons, like electrical faults. Wear and tear over time also contributes. Common issues include overheating, which may occur if the inverter is exposed to direct sunlight. Adequate ventilation is also important here. Faulty wiring or loose connections can also lead to short circuits or improper energy conversion.
Power surges caused by lightning strikes or fluctuations in the grid can damage the inverter’s components. Regular monitoring and maintenance, such as cleaning vents, checking for error codes, and inspecting electrical connections, can help prevent these issues and ensure optimal performance of the solar inverter.
The cost of replacing solar panels can vary widely depending on several factors, including the size and type of the system, labor costs, and geographic location. On average, replacing a single solar panel can cost between $200 and $500, not including installation. If many panels need to be replaced or if extra repairs to the system are required. The total expenses can increase significantly if left unchecked.
Arizona homeowners should also consider any warranties or insurance coverage that may offset replacement costs. To get an accurate estimate, it is advisable to consult with Solar Topps, who can assess the specific needs and provide a detailed quote.
The size of your solar panel system plays a significant role in determining its cost. Larger systems, which are designed to generate more electricity, need more solar panels, inverters, and installation materials. This naturally increases both the upfront installation costs and the labor required.
Conversely, smaller systems are less expensive but may not fully meet the energy needs of a larger household or business. You should test your energy consumption patterns carefully to determine the appropriate system size.

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

Over time, battery storage capacity declines, resulting in shorter backup duration and less reliable power during outages.
Aging batteries often trigger fault codes, communication issues, or inconsistent charging behavior that can compromise system performance.
Newer battery backup systems offer higher usable capacity, faster response times, improved safety features, and better whole-home backup capabilities.
Charge your battery from the grid when energy is cheapest and protect your home from rate hikes, peak pricing, demand fees and unpredictable power outages. Lower your utility bill and offset rising electricity costs with a battery-only energy system from Solar Topps. Whether a new installation or an addition to an existing system, we’ve got you covered.
Contact for a Free Site EvaluationCustomers choose Solar Topps because replacing a battery backup system is an engineering project—not a simple swap. Our team includes in-house engineers and senior technicians with hands-on experience across legacy battery systems, mixed inverter platforms, partial and whole-home backup configurations, and utility-specific interconnection requirements.
We understand how batteries integrate with existing solar arrays, load centers, transfer switches, and monitoring software, and we design each replacement to function safely, efficiently, and reliably within your current infrastructure.
We routinely handle complex replacement scenarios—including discontinued equipment, undersized or improperly designed original systems, service panel constraints, and homeowners upgrading from partial backup to whole-home backup. Because we maintain an active battery inventory and supporting hardware, we can respond quickly without compromising on system design or electrical standards. A well-maintained solar battery will perform better and last longer. Here’s how to extend the life of your new battery:
By following these recommendations, you’ll maximize both your savings and your battery’s lifespan.
Replacing a solar battery typically costs between $5,000 and $15,000, depending on factors like battery type, capacity, and installation complexity. Lithium-ion batteries are more expensive but offer better efficiency and longevity than lead-acid options. Get a quote from a certified installer like Solar Topps.
Battery Type: Lithium-ion batteries are more expensive upfront but offer a better ROI over time due to their durability and efficiency.
Capacity Requirement: Larger-capacity batteries cost more but store more energy.
Labor Costs: Installation fees depend on local rates and the complexity of the replacement.
Warranty Coverage: Some solar batteries come with warranties that may partially offset replacement costs.
A residential solar battery is a device that stores the excess energy produced by your solar panels during the day. This stored energy can be used:
By replacing traditional energy usage with solar power stored in a reliable battery, you maximize the return on your solar investment. However, like all batteries, solar batteries have a limited lifespan, requiring replacement to maintain your system’s efficiency.
One common main wiring issue is improper grounding. Grounding refers to the process of connecting all metal parts of a solar power system to an external grounding rod or conductor. This helps prevent electric shock and damage from lightning strikes. If your solar battery is not properly grounded, it can lead to safety hazards and potential damage to your system.
Identifying improper grounding involves inspecting the wiring and connections of your solar power system. Look for loose or disconnected wires, particularly those connected to the grounding rod.
Testing with a multimeter can verify proper conductivity and ensure that the system is safely grounded. Anomalies in the performance of your solar battery, such as unexpected surges or frequent tripping of circuit breakers, may also indicate grounding issues.
Resolving grounding issues requires careful attention to safety and compliance with electrical codes. Start by turning off the system’s power before making adjustments. Securely connect all grounding wires to the designated grounding rod, ensuring a solid and unobstructed connection.
If you’re unsure of how to proceed, consulting a licensed technician or electrician is highly recommended to avoid risks and ensure the longevity of your system. Regular system inspections can also help prevent grounding issues from recurring.

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

An aging or failing solar inverter can significantly reduce the amount of usable energy your system produces. Replacing an outdated inverter restores optimal performance, improves energy conversion efficiency, and helps your solar panels deliver maximum power to your home.
Most solar inverters have a lifespan of 8–12 years. As they age, they become more prone to breakdowns, error codes, and complete system shutdowns. Proactively replacing your inverter helps prevent costly repairs, lost energy production, and unexpected power disruptions.
Modern solar inverters are designed to support battery storage systems, EV chargers, and whole-home backup solutions. If your current inverter is not compatible, upgrading is essential to expand your system and protect your home during grid outages.
New inverter technology provides real-time system monitoring, performance alerts, and remote diagnostics. These features make it easier to track energy usage, identify issues early, and ensure your solar system is operating at peak performance year-round.
