Qualified solar professionals will ensure a seamless installation, correct inverter sizing, and proper calibration for your existing system. We can help you select a model that matches your energy goals and budget while adhering to local electrical codes and utility requirements.
A holistic solar energy system is more than just panels and an inverter; it’s an integrated solution designed to maximize energy production, efficiency, and reliability. Properly designed systems take into account factors such as roof orientation, shading, energy consumption patterns, and potential future expansion needs. This comprehensive approach ensures that your solar investment delivers the highest return over its lifespan while reducing your carbon footprint. Regular maintenance and system monitoring are also critical components, as they help identify and resolve issues early, preserving system performance and longevity.
Solar inverters typically have a lifespan of 10 to 15 years, depending on the brand, model, and environmental factors. However, several signs may indicate it is time to replace your inverter. If your system’s energy production has noticeably decreased or you experience frequent shutdowns, your inverter may no longer be performing efficiently. Error messages or warning lights on the inverter display are also clear indicators of potential issues.
Regular maintenance and monitoring of your solar system can help identify these problems early and prevent further disruptions. Proactively addressing inverter replacement ensures that your solar energy system operates at peak performance, maximizing your investment over time.
While inverters are a critical component, it is equally important to monitor the condition of your solar panels. Physical damage, such as cracks, discoloration, or hotspots on the panels, can significantly reduce energy output. Accumulation of dirt, debris, or snow may also obstruct sunlight and hinder performance. Regular visual inspections can help detect these issues early and ensure that your panels are functioning optimally. If any abnormalities are observed, it is advisable to contact Solar Topps for further evaluation and repair. Maintaining the integrity of your solar panels is essential for sustaining the overall efficiency and longevity of your solar energy system.
Several signs may indicate your solar inverter is not functioning correctly. One of the most common is a lack of power generation, which can often be identified through your system’s monitoring software. If your energy production is significantly lower than usual, this could point to an issue with your inverter.
Physical signs such as unusual noises or overheating of the inverter unit could indicate internal malfunctions. Inspecting the inverter for visible damage, such as corrosion or wear, is also an important step in diagnosing potential problems. If you suspect your inverter is faulty, contact Solar Topps for a thorough assessment is crucial to restoring your solar system’s functionality.
String inverters are a popular choice for residential and small commercial solar systems. They work by linking a series of solar panels (called a “string”) to one inverter, which converts all the DC electricity from the panels into usable AC electricity. They’re affordable and pretty easy to install, but there’s a catch—if one panel in the string is shaded or not performing well, it can impact the performance of the whole system.
Microinverters are installed on each solar panel, converting DC to AC electricity directly at the panel. This allows each panel to operate independently, so one underperforming panel won’t affect the rest. While they cost more upfront, microinverters offer better efficiency and monitoring, making them ideal for systems with shading or varied panel orientations.
Power optimizers are used alongside traditional string inverters and are installed on individual solar panels. Their function is to optimize the DC electricity generated by each panel before transferring it to the central inverter for AC conversion. This technology offers a balance between the advantages of microinverters—such as enhanced performance in shaded conditions—and the cost efficiency of a string inverter.
Hybrid inverters, or multi-mode inverters, combine the functions of grid-tied and battery inverters. They let solar energy power your home, send excess energy to the grid, and store energy in a battery. Perfect for homeowners adding solar storage, hybrid inverters are flexible and growing in popularity as battery technology improves.
Off-grid inverters convert DC electricity from solar panels or batteries into AC power for homes or businesses without grid access. Commonly used in remote areas, they often include features to manage battery charging and discharging. Choosing the right inverter depends on system design, budget, and energy needs.

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.
This process can take longer than expected. Everything that I encountered with delays had nothing to do with them. But I blamed them in the moment. They listened and never got upset with me.
In the end, I was happy with the system they designed based on the info I gave them. After installing, my goals started changing, and I dug deep into usage. Put an energy monitor in my main panel on every circuit to see what uses what in the house. I then changed what I could to lower the usage.
I now have added 2 more Tesla Powerwall expansion batteries. I use zero power from APS and sell them nearly 4 bucks a day in power. It's nice to get paid by them and not pay them. Also, they can raise the rates all they want.t I don't use their power anymore.
Thanks, Niel, Sean, Robby, Summy, Mike, Gaurav
I have turned into a total solar geek. Thanks Solar Topps!!!!

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

Older solar monitoring systems often provide limited or inaccurate data, making it difficult to detect underperforming panels, inverter issues, or system outages. Upgrading your monitoring system gives you real-time visibility into energy production, helping ensure your solar system is actually delivering the savings you expect.
Modern solar monitoring platforms offer advanced alerts, error reporting, and remote diagnostics. This allows problems to be identified and addressed quickly—often before they result in extended downtime or lost energy production.
Many legacy monitoring systems are not compatible with newer inverter technology, battery storage, or system expansions. Replacing the monitoring system ensures seamless integration with current and future upgrades, including whole-home backup and smart energy management tools.
Today’s monitoring systems provide user-friendly apps, detailed performance history, and clear insights into energy usage and savings. An upgraded system gives homeowners greater control, transparency, and confidence that their solar investment is operating efficiently year after year.
When customers choose Solar Topps to upgrade or replace their solar monitoring system, they’re choosing accuracy, expertise, and long-term confidence in their solar investment. Monitoring upgrades aren’t just about installing a new app—they require deep understanding of inverter communication, system architecture, and utility interconnection. Solar Topps evaluates your entire system to ensure the new monitoring device is fully compatible, properly configured, and delivering meaningful, reliable data. Our team installs and commissions monitoring systems in-house, verifies real-time production, and ensures alerts and reporting are set up correctly so homeowners can actually use the information to protect performance.
We also specialize in working with older and mixed-equipment systems, where monitoring issues are most common. Whether your current platform is no longer supported, producing inaccurate data, or failing to integrate with batteries or backup systems, Solar Topps designs a solution that fits your system today while preparing it for future upgrades. With readily available equipment, experienced technicians, and a process built around precision and accountability, we minimize downtime and restore visibility into your energy production quickly.
Ultimately, customers choose Solar Topps because we don’t just replace a device—we deliver clarity. Our monitoring upgrades provide actionable insights, early issue detection, and confidence that your solar system is operating efficiently, safely, and as intended for years to come.

1 Year ago, you couldn't talk me into solar. I thought it was a scam. At the beginning of 2025, I started seeing videos about solar with a battery. I got interested. I got 9 quotes from different companies. Solar Topps wasn't the cheapest, but it was truly one of the few that was local to the valley. This was important to have a local company involved and not a company that is nationwide using a contractor. One thing I learned fast is that ALL Solar Topps employees live here in the valley. Solar Topps turned out to be the best. Very organized and helpful. Also, Solar Topps designed the best system they could using APS bills. But really, they need more information to dial the system in to your usage. So do your homework and stop blaming them because you didnt give them all the pcs of the puzzle.
Also, when you're new to Solar, the customer has to define their goals to help them. I thought I knew what my goals were. I later learned my goal has changed. I started with a 50-panel 20Kwh system with 1 Powerwall 3 whole-home backup battery. I thought I would never have to buy power from APS again. It wasn't till I started going day by day at my usage and pulling my after-hours, meaning no solar production to see just how many batteries I really need to achieve this. Most people don't know this data.

This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the...
This review is for a rooftop solar combined with Tesla Powerwall 3 install.
I had been considering solar for some time, but sticker shock from the APS rate increases finally pushed me to act. I knew I wanted to own the panels instead of getting locked into some weird lease system. Fortunately, I knew Mark Greene through work and asked his advice. He works with Solar Topps and was able to sit down with my family and clearly explain the pros and cons of different options, and give us a detailed picture of what we could expect. We decided it was a good move for us and signed up.
Once the process began, it went pretty much exactly as Mark described. The installers were very professional and efficient. They work directly for the company (not subcontractors) so the communication was quick and easy and their truck was clearly labeled Solar Topps. They left the work area clean when they were done and the black on black solar panels look very nice and modern.
The regulation process through the City of Phoenix and APS was definitely slow but at least proceeded smoothly. Solar Topps kept us informed of next steps and what to expect for a general timeline. So that part was as painless as possible.
Now that the system is turned on and running we are very satisfied with the results. The Tesla app makes everything about your power use and generation very clear. When nothing is turned on you can see the baseline power your house uses, and the when the heater or airconditioning turns on you can see the use jump up, which is informative. Also you can easily see how much power use was solar, battery, and grid along with a cost savings estimate.
So over all, I would highly recommend talking to Mark to get a good idea of what your different options are, and I would trust Solar Topps to give you a clean and efficient install and setup. Just keep in mind that your city and APS/SRP are going to take a while to inspect and approve everything. After that, enjoy making your own power, saving money and being secure from blackouts.

We shopped carefully once we decided to finally install a solar panel system. We nearly signed a contract with a national company and hesitated once we found out they didn't have a local subcontractor to actually install the system and would, instead, have a company travel from Tucson to Cave Creek.
We contacted a few local companies and also used Energy Sage online to get some quotes. Two responses from Energy Sage included Solar Topps and we're glad they did.
Solar Topps gave us a price equal to the lowest national quote and the hardware was better (Panasonic panels versus something else) and good Enphase electronics. They were also a couple thousand dollars less than another local company we had install our solar hot water heater system.
We had a signed contract with Solar Topps dated March 9 and our system was turned on and working April 12.
That, to us, is an incredibly fast turnaround for a good sized solar panel system. We had been prepared by other companies for a 90 day period of time start to finish, so to have it done in a few days more than A MONTH was a very pleasant surprise.
We didn't have to do ANY of the paperwork with Maricopa County or APS, Solar Topps took care of all of it in a painless fashion.
Solar Topps was a pleasure to work with every step of the way. Any questions were answered via phone or email VERY promptly and correctly.
An example:
Our system has panels oriented south and west. Solar Topps was the only company to come up with this option to maximize the efficiency of our system to take advantage of the peak power rates of APS by having some panels installed to maximize the efficiency of the total system in the afternoon when the sun is lower in the west. See the attached real-time report from our panels and an early billing report from APS where our first few days with the system running has APS paying US instead of vice-versa. (to be fair, the weather has been easy and the A/C hasn't been running, but... still that's pretty cool)
If you are thinking of solar and you're in the Phoenix metro area (or elsewhere, even), you should definitely give SERIOUS consideration to using local company around for a long time Solar Topps.
Seriously, DO IT!
